note: One Fable 5.2 agent at high effort judged all 39 disagreements, reading only the judge packet.

verdicts.reason: The stylesheet URL comes from the proxy operator's own rule values, and anyone able to write those rules can already inject arbitrary HTML and script into proxied pages, so the unescaped href crosses no trust boundary.

The LDAP-sourced login is printed into an attribute value and the page body with no dol_escape_htmltag (unlike the GETPOST branch beside it), and directory attributes are external data that directory users or delegated admins can set.

The only tainted piece is $_SERVER['PHP_SELF'], which Dolibarr's main.inc.php rejects when it contains a double quote or semicolon, so the double-quoted href cannot be broken out of, and the id is numeric.
showdocuments receives sanitized file names, a numeric id and a PHP_SELF value that main.inc.php already screens for quotes, so nothing attacker-shaped reaches the printed HTML.
The form action only carries PHP_SELF, which main.inc.php blocks if it contains a double quote or script patterns, so path-info cannot escape the attribute.
The href is PHP_SELF (screened centrally for double quotes in main.inc.php) plus a numeric object id, leaving no way to break out of the attribute.

req.url is concatenated unescaped into a text/html 404 body and an href with no server-side encoding at all, and relying on browsers to percent-encode the request target is not a validation in this code.
SetInGroup concatenates $group and $entity into DELETE and INSERT statements with no int cast, and the user card passes an unfiltered GETPOST('entity') in multicompany transverse mode.

Order is whitelisted and the limit is int-cast, but the content-type list is interpolated into IN (...) after an unshown split() and the packet does not show whether that string comes from field configuration or from a request.
table_name is the first WebDAV path segment, but exists() checks it against SHOW TABLES before any resource is built or DESCRIBE is issued, so only real table names reach this statement.

hostId is a crypto.randomUUID and the island script body is generated by the framework from encrypted props and script-safe serialization (stringifyForScript), so no raw request or user text is shown reaching the script tag.

srcSchema and targetSchema are interpolated raw into a double-quoted shell string run through exec, and schema names come from backup or collection metadata that a backup uploader can shape, with no shell quoting anywhere.

The checkpoint name supplied through the workflow API is joined into the checkpoint directory as f'{name}.json' and opened for writing with no separator or containment check, so a name with ../ writes outside the directory.

The SSID is passed through util.sanitizeString immediately before being placed inside the quoted netsh argument, which is a deliberate sanitizing step and nothing shown suggests it leaves quotes or metacharacters in.
$filter is a developer-facing SQL-fragment parameter and the in-tree callers build it from constants or int-filtered values, with no request-controlled path shown.

delete_session is a public method that joins the caller-supplied session name into a path and unlinks it with no sanitization or containment check, so ../ in a session name deletes .json files outside the sessions folder.

Project ref and title are user-entered values read from the database, and Project::getNomUrl emits the ref unescaped as link text (title only partly escaped for the tooltip), so a stored value with markup renders in this list.
The script URL comes from the operator's own proxy rules, whose purpose is to inject scripts into pages, so an unescaped src value gives the rule author nothing they did not already have.
output_path is taken straight from workflow params and used for makedirs and save with no base-directory confinement visible, so a workflow can write image files to arbitrary locations.
The query uses a slug from a configured ContentType object, an order string forced through fixOrder's whitelist and an int-typed amount, so no request-controlled SQL text reaches it.
RemoveFromGroup concatenates $group and $entity into the DELETE with no cast or escaping, and the user card passes an unfiltered GETPOST('entity') in multicompany transverse mode.
$i is a server-side integer counter and the $_GET['order'] value is only handed to select_input, which emits it through optionlist or h() escaping.
$ldap_lastname from the directory is printed into a hidden input's value and the body with no escaping, so a crafted directory attribute injects markup into the admin's create-user page.

Although escape($rid) is used unquoted, the callers in the permissions pages pass an int-filtered rights id and the entity defaults to the configured entity, while module and perms come from the rights_def table.
$ldap_mail from the directory is written into a hidden input value with no HTML escaping, so a directory-controlled mail attribute can break out of the attribute.
The name attribute uses an integer counter and the $_GET['columns'] value passes through select_input, which escapes the selected value, so no raw request text is echoed here.

The only value interpolated into this command is the number-typed limit with a default of 50, and the string taskName is used only to filter output in JavaScript, so no string input is shown reaching the shell.
$ldap_mobile from the directory is printed straight into the page body with no escaping, which is HTML injection from externally controlled directory data.
$ldap_mail from the directory is printed straight into the page body with no escaping, the same unescaped directory-data sink as its sibling fields.
The link contains only PHP_SELF, which main.inc.php rejects when it holds a double quote, and a numeric id, so the href cannot be broken out of.
getGitHash is a private helper and the only caller shown passes the literal 'HEAD', so no caller-influenced ref is shown reaching the shell string.

The unquoted escape($rid) is a weak pattern, but the permissions pages pass an int-filtered rights id and the entity defaults to the configured entity, so no injectable string reaches this query in practice.

Markdown link destinations are user input, the safeMode scheme check runs on the raw destination before backslash resolution and normalization, and with safeMode off there is no scheme check at all, so a javascript: href can be emitted.
This converts an admin-supplied Revue import into post HTML, and the importing admin can already publish arbitrary HTML and script in posts, so the unescaped url crosses no privilege boundary.
Only PHP_SELF (screened for double quotes in main.inc.php) and a numeric id are printed in this link.
This is the query builder's generic batch executor running SQL rendered internally from escaped values and protected identifiers, and no unvalidated input is shown entering the statement.
The image src is normalized and escaped and a script scheme in an img src does not execute, while the alt text is tag-stripped rendered output, so no working injection is shown at this line.

sessionId comes straight from req.query and is path.join'ed into the log path, and because path.join collapses 'session-log-x/../..' lexically, a crafted id reads .jsonl files outside the hooks data directory.
formconfirm is given PHP_SELF, which main.inc.php blocks if it contains a double quote or semicolon, plus a numeric id and static translations.
